narrative: The model estimates your chance of failing the final year at 29.0%, roughly three in ten. Although that is not a majority, it is high enough for the model to place you in the fail category, which is why remedial courses are required as a precaution rather than as a certainty. The strongest factor behind the prediction was your history of past class failures: you have none, compared with an average of zero among students who passed, and this pushed the prediction toward passing. The second strongest factor was your very low free time after school, which also pushed toward passing; only about 7% of passing students had very low free time. The third factor was your mother’s education level: primary education pushed toward failing, since only about 14% of passing students had a mother with primary education, while higher education was much more common. That is background, not a measure of your ability. To improve, protect your record of no failures, keep a steady study routine, and seek support early through teachers, school resources, family, or tutoring. Also watch attendance: six absences is above the passing average of about 3.8, so attending consistently is a practical next step.
